purpose: Sanitized fixture corpus for future story-only output evaluation. It supplies authority and expected developments; it does not record model-quality results.

requirements: Score all 12 cases across all five dimensions.
No output may contain mechanics language or violate fiction authority.
future_acceptance_gate.note: This gate applies only to an explicitly authorized future live-quality evaluation; this corpus records no scores or quality result.

direction_fidelity.0: misses or reverses a required direction

next_choice_relevance.0: choices do not follow the narrated moment
next_choice_relevance.2: all choices offer immediate grounded developments

distinctness.2: four choices and suggestion are clearly distinct

world_facts: The river gate opens only when its brass keeper recognizes a spoken promise.
Keeper Orin lost his sister Mara during the last flood.
continuity: Mara's blue ribbon was found caught in the gate mechanism.
Orin has refused all travelers since dawn.
open_threads: Learn why the ribbon is warm despite the cold water.

input.direction: Speak with Orin beside the flooded gate and show him Mara's ribbon.

required_claims: Orin and the blue ribbon are present at the gate.
The exchange acknowledges Orin's connection to Mara.
forbidden_claims: The gate opens before Orin recognizes a promise.
Mara is declared alive or dead without new evidence.
Any roll, score, check, or hidden-mechanics explanation.
expected_next_developments: Offer a promise Orin might recognize.
Ask what Mara said during the last flood.
Examine why the ribbon is warm.

world_facts: The abandoned skyrail has three lantern stations between the market and the observatory.
Only a lit lantern marks a safe plank crossing.
continuity: The first lantern has gone dark.
A courier map marks a side stair below station two.
open_threads: Reach the observatory before the storm covers the rail.

input.direction: Relight the first lantern, take the side stair at station two, and arrive at the observatory roof.

required_claims: The narration includes relighting the first lantern before using the side stair.
The narration actually reaches the observatory roof after the stated route.
forbidden_claims: Skipping directly from the market to the roof.
Inventing a fourth lantern station.
Any mechanics terminology.
expected_next_developments: Inspect the storm instruments on the roof.
Search for the courier who marked the map.
Decide whether to secure the rail behind the party.

world_facts: Glass footprints appear only in the conservatory after midnight.
The conservatory has no exterior doors; its roof vents are sealed.
continuity: Three glass prints lead from the fern room to a locked seed vault.
The curator's silver key has been missing for two days.
open_threads: Identify who leaves the glass footprints.

input.direction: Follow the glass footprints to the seed vault and inspect the lock without forcing it.

required_claims: The seed vault remains locked unless new authority supports opening it.
The glass prints and missing silver key remain relevant clues.
forbidden_claims: Naming the culprit as fact.
Opening the vault by force.
Claiming an exterior intruder entered through a sealed vent.
expected_next_developments: Compare the lock with the curator's key description.
Look for reflections or residue near the prints.
Question the curator about access to the vault.

world_facts: Cartographer Sela is traveling beyond the salt flats and cannot be contacted today.
Her workshop contains only copied maps, never her original field journal.
continuity: A red pin on Sela's wall map marks the old well.
A neighbor heard a wind chime in the empty workshop at noon.
open_threads: Find what Sela wanted at the old well.

input.direction: Search Sela's workshop for a clue to the old well.

required_claims: Sela remains absent.
The red pin and copied maps can be examined as available clues.
forbidden_claims: Sela appears, speaks, or sends a new message.
Her original field journal is found in the workshop.
Mechanics language.
expected_next_developments: Trace a copied route toward the old well.
Investigate the noon wind chime.
Ask the neighbor what they saw near the workshop.

world_facts: The harbor bell controls the fog signal.
The bell tower overlooks the eastern docks.
continuity: The cracked bell rope has already been repaired.
The fog signal sounded once and the trapped ferry reached harbor.
open_threads: Discover who cut the rope before the storm.

input.direction: Return to the bell tower and make sure the ferry can finally enter the harbor.

required_claims: The ferry's safe arrival and repaired rope remain completed events.
The scene investigates evidence of the prior rope sabotage rather than repeating the rescue.
forbidden_claims: Repairing the rope again.
Claiming the ferry is still trapped in fog.
Undoing the completed rescue.
expected_next_developments: Examine the cut fibers for a clue.
Speak with the ferry crew about what they saw.
Check who had access to the tower before the storm.

world_facts: The quarry lies west of the village; the archive lies under the town hall.
continuity: The party left the quarry at sunset.
They are now inside the archive's map room with a damp stone shard.
open_threads: Match the shard's markings to an archive map.

input.direction: Study the damp stone shard with the map room's lamp.

required_claims: The current scene remains in the archive map room.
The damp stone shard is available for study.
forbidden_claims: The party is suddenly back at the quarry.
The quarry collapses during this archive scene.
Any unannounced travel.
expected_next_developments: Compare the markings with a map legend.
Search the archive for records of the quarry.
Follow a marked route from the map room.

world_facts: The Moon Door can open only beneath moonlight and never at sunrise.
Its inscription is visible only after the door opens.
continuity: Dawn has begun over the eastern ridge.
The party has a chalk copy of the door's outer sigil.
open_threads: Learn what the Moon Door protects.

input.direction: Open the Moon Door at sunrise and read the inscription inside.

required_claims: The narration acknowledges that sunrise prevents opening the Moon Door.
The chalk copy remains a usable clue.
forbidden_claims: The Moon Door opens at sunrise.
The inside inscription is read.
A new exception to the moonlight rule.
expected_next_developments: Prepare to return under moonlight.
Study the chalk sigil for a clue.
Seek a witness who knows the door's history.

world_facts: The archivist's raven understands gestures but does not speak.
The archive reading room is quiet and open to visitors.
continuity: The raven holds a brass tag in its beak.
The tag bears only the number 17.
open_threads: Find the record associated with tag 17.

required_claims: The raven and brass tag 17 remain present.
The response treats the signal as open to plausible interpretation rather than inventing a precise command.
forbidden_claims: Claiming the raven speaks words.
Claiming the player requested a specific shelf without evidence.
Mechanics language.
expected_next_developments: Offer a hand or an object to the raven.
Search the catalog for 17.
Follow the raven if it moves through the reading room.

world_facts: The old bridge crosses the Alder Run.
A brass lantern hangs beneath its center span.
The bridge bell rings only after a red boat docks.
continuity: The party is standing on the north bank at dusk.
No red boat has docked.
open_threads: Find out who maintains the lantern under the bridge.

input.direction: Walk under the bridge and inspect the brass lantern.

required_claims: The lantern and north-bank approach are used.
The dormant bell event remains inactive because its stated condition is absent.
forbidden_claims: A red boat docks.
The bell rings.
The dormant event is resolved or removed.
expected_next_developments: Examine the lantern's maker mark.
Look for a maintenance path along the bank.
Ask nearby boatkeepers about the lantern.

world_facts: A clockwork orchard has a locked copper gate and four pear-shaped keys hanging nearby.
continuity: One key is warm, while the other three are cold.
The gate has not been opened.
open_threads: Determine which key belongs in the copper gate.

input.direction: Consider the warm key at the copper gate.
candidate_choices: Try the warm key in the gate.
Inspect the cold keys for markings.
Look for scratches around the lock.
input.candidate_custom_action_suggestion: try THE warm key in the gate.

required_claims: The warm key and unopened copper gate remain central.
A repaired custom suggestion must differ from every choice after normalization.
forbidden_claims: Accepting the candidate custom suggestion as distinct.
Opening the gate without choosing or narrating a supported action.
Mechanics language.
expected_next_developments: Compare key temperatures.
Inspect the lock's scratches.
Choose a distinct way to investigate the orchard.

continuity: A paper crane rests on the cabinet latch.
The crane contains a folded note bearing the word café.
The ledger is still closed.
open_threads: Learn why the paper crane was left on the cabinet.

input.direction: Inspect the paper crane on the blue cabinet.
candidate_choices: Read the café note folded inside the paper crane.
Wait for the proprietor to return.
Search the delivery cart for a matching seal.

A repair treats canonically equivalent Unicode, case, and whitespace duplicates as invalid.

Opening the closed ledger without support.
Mechanics language.
expected_next_developments: Study the crane's fold pattern.
Inspect the latch without opening the ledger.
Ask the proprietor about the delivery seal.
